clue.text: High explosive island queen

parts.note: Cuba is the large Caribbean island

explanation.surface: A dangerous queen of an island, armed with high explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend she was the wife of Priam, king of Troy, so a royal consort.

clue.text: Useful furniture for the hanger-on

parts.note: hanger-on reads as a sponger but means a coat or hat to be hung up

explanation.surface: Handy furnishings for a parasite.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hanger-on' is usually a sycophant; here it is anything hung on a stand in the entrance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand with pegs in an entrance passage for coats, hats and umbrellas.

clue.text: Something with which to deck a C.O.

definitions.text: Something with which to deck a C.O.

parts.words: Something with which to deck a C.O.
parts.note: deck means adorn, not knock down; a commanding officer might wear a rosette on his hat

explanation.surface: A means of punching out one's commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' sounds like flooring someone; here it means decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette or knot of ribbon worn on a hat as a badge of rank or party.

clue.text: Certain globe-trotters make sport of it

definitions.text: Certain globe-trotters make sport of it

parts.words: Certain globe-trotters make sport of it
parts.note: the Harlem Globetrotters are a touring exhibition team famed for clowning on court

explanation.surface: Some world travellers mock something.
explanation.walkthrough: The Harlem Globetrotters are an American touring team; 'make sport of' means both play and ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: The court game played by the Harlem Globetrotters, with hoops and a large ball.

clue.text: Her toast, perhaps, is " The Resistance Movement "

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of her toast may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A woman raises her glass to the wartime underground fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a toast to the wartime Resistance; the definition really describes a device that varies (moves) electrical resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A variable resistor in a circuit, whose slider shifts the amount of electrical resistance.

clue.text: Serpentine nymph

definitions.meaning: as a noun, a snake: the king cobra of India
a wood nymph living in a tree, in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A snakelike spirit of the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serpentine' looks like an adjective for the nymph, but it is a separate definition naming the king cobra; in Britain the Serpentine is also a lake in Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the king cobra and a tree-dwelling dryad of Greek myth bear the name.

clue.text: This man is in the furniture line

definitions.text: This man is in the furniture line

parts.words: This man is in the furniture line
parts.note: a male name which, with 'man' after it, makes a piece of furniture, a padded seat

explanation.surface: A fellow works in the furniture trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Add 'man' to the name and you get OTTOMAN, a low upholstered seat; 'This man' is the name in front of 'man'.
explanation.definitionFit: A German male forename, the first part of a cushioned footstool's name.

clue.text: Here tan can be acquired in the city

indicators.note: the letters of here tan are acquired in a new order, like a tan picked up in the sun

explanation.surface: A suntan is to be had in this hot capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The text held read 'can' for 'tan'; the scan shows 'Here tan'. TEHERAN is the older spelling of Tehran.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Iran, in its older spelling.

clue.text: Namely, what to do with a broken-down car

definitions.meaning: that is to say, introducing an example

definitions.text: what to do with a broken-down car
definitions.meaning: a car that will not run must be pulled by another vehicle

explanation.surface: Explaining what happens to a car that has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as TOW IT for the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An old legal phrase for 'that is to say', and, split, the instruction to haul a disabled vehicle.

clue.text: Retreat by rail, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of rail might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Withdrawing by train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A den or hideaway to which a wild animal withdraws.

clue.text: Lovelace wrote to her going beyond the seas

definitions.text: Lovelace wrote to her going beyond the seas

parts.words: Lovelace wrote to her going beyond the seas
parts.note: points to the Cavalier poet Richard Lovelace and his poem addressed to a lady as he went overseas

explanation.surface: A poet writes to his sweetheart as he sails abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is 'To Lucasta, Going beyond the Seas' by Richard Lovelace (1618-1657).
explanation.definitionFit: The lady named in the title of the seventeenth-century poem by Richard Lovelace.

clue.text: His custom was to receive it

definitions.text: His custom was to receive it

parts.words: His custom was to receive it
parts.note: custom here means tax or customs duty, not habit: the apostle was a tax collector sitting at the receipt of custom

explanation.surface: A man whose habit was to accept something.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Gospel the apostle is called while 'sitting at the receipt of custom', that is, collecting taxes; 'custom' reads as habit.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle and evangelist was a publican, a collector of tolls and duties, before following Jesus.

clue.text: Uncle Tom and others supplied its merchandise

definitions.text: Uncle Tom and others supplied its merchandise

parts.words: Uncle Tom and others supplied its merchandise
parts.note: Uncle Tom is the enslaved hero of Harriet Beecher Stowe's novel; people like him were what this commerce sold

explanation.surface: A fictional character and his companions provide goods for a business.
explanation.definitionFit: The commerce in human beings, whose goods were enslaved people such as the hero of Uncle Tom's Cabin.

clue.text: To run back would be legally wrong

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for a legal wrong from right to left

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Turning tail would be against the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses TORT; 'would be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To move at a jogging pace, a gentle running gait.

clue.text: Stevenson's dark missile

parts.note: black means dark
an arrow is a missile shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A Scottish author's sinister projectile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stevenson's' stands for a work of his: Robert Louis Stevenson's 1888 novel of the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a novel by Robert Louis Stevenson.

clue.text: Still out-of-date

parts.note: still is the distilling apparatus, not the adverb; this kind is an antiquated one used by alchemists

explanation.surface: Something remains old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adverb ('even now out-of-date') but is the noun for distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned distilling vessel of the alchemists, now obsolete.

clue.text: Weapons for use against the Amazons ?

definitions.text: Weapons for use against the Amazons ?

parts.words: Weapons for use against the Amazons ?
parts.note: the Amazons were a race of warrior women, so a weapon against them would be one that wounds girls

explanation.surface: Arms suitable for fighting legendary women warriors.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as CUT LASSES: blades that would cut the Amazon women.
explanation.definitionFit: Short curved swords used by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Name one lady perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of one lady could form something else

explanation.surface: Give a woman's name, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, a forename.

clue.text: Far from hard currency

parts.note: hard currency means stable foreign money; the opposite of hard here is cash got without effort

explanation.surface: A weak, unreliable kind of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard currency' is a financial term for stable money; the opposite of 'hard' read as difficult gives money easily earned.
explanation.definitionFit: Money gained with little effort.

clue.text: Garment for a total abstainer ?

parts.note: a total abstainer is teetotal, TT

explanation.surface: Clothing suited to someone who never drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the abbreviation for teetotal; the answer splits as DOUBLE T. It is also a close-fitting man's jacket of Tudor times.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting jacket worn by men from the fourteenth to seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: Not a prey to woolgathering

parts.note: woolgathering means daydreaming but here a sheep's fleece has not been gathered by shears

explanation.surface: Someone who never lets the mind wander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woolgathering' means absent-minded daydreaming; literally, a sheep not yet clipped has not been a prey to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Not having had the fleece or hair clipped.

clue.text: Two of them comprise 30 years !

parts.note: each is a span of ten years; the exclamation marks that the arithmetic is not straightforward

explanation.surface: A puzzling sum about spans of time.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the figures do not add up: two ten-year spans make twenty years and three make thirty. The page reads 30, so the arithmetic is the setter's.
explanation.definitionFit: Periods of ten years each.

clue.text: Soldier in transvestite attire and a pair of spectacles going North

parts.note: drag is clothing of the opposite sex
spectacles look like two round O's

explanation.surface: A cross-dressed soldier with glasses heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'going' are links; the two lenses are drawn as OO.
explanation.definitionFit: A mounted infantryman, a cavalry trooper.

clue.text: This master is not necessarily a "has-been "

definitions.text: This master is not necessarily a "has-been "

parts.words: This master is not necessarily a "has-been "
parts.note: the word before master looks as if it means a former one

explanation.surface: A master craftsman need not be washed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Past master' means an expert, not someone whose time is over, though 'past' alone suggests a has-been.
explanation.definitionFit: The word that goes before master in the phrase for an expert, and which elsewhere means bygone.

clue.text: A bird gets it with seed

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed

explanation.surface: A small bird picks up something along with its seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown songbird such as the meadow or tree species.

clue.text: Wolf-cry

parts.note: the fable of the boy who cried wolf: a shout of danger when there is none

explanation.surface: The howl of a wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: In Aesop's fable the shepherd boy cries 'Wolf!' when no wolf is there.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning given when there is no real danger, as the shepherd boy did.

clue.text: One has it to kneel on, or wear

definitions.text: One has it to kneel on, or wear

parts.words: One has it to kneel on, or wear
parts.note: putting 'has' before the word gives a church kneeling cushion; on its own it is something worn on the foot

explanation.surface: A thing you kneel on or put on.
explanation.walkthrough: HAS + SOCK makes HASSOCK, the cushion to kneel on in church; the plain word is worn on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted covering for the foot, and the second half of a kneeling cushion's name.

clue.text: A cad bruised by the serpent

definitions.meaning: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter
in Genesis 3:15 God tells the serpent that man shall bruise its head and it shall bruise his foot's back

explanation.surface: A rogue harmed by a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition refers to Genesis 3:15: 'thou shalt bruise his heel'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel, and the back of the foot bitten by the snake in Genesis.

clue.text: Birds for soft-headed sweethearts

parts.note: soft is p, piano, in music; headed puts it at the front
sweethearts are lovers

explanation.surface: Birds as a present for foolish couples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft-headed' looks like 'foolish' but gives P (piano, soft) at the head of LOVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Wading birds such as the lapwing, also called peewits.

clue.text: Picture of a carrier with nothing on

parts.note: a cart carries goods
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An image of a porter wearing no clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing on' suggests nakedness, but it is O followed by ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing, especially a humorous one or a design for a painting.

clue.text: Not giving oneself airs

parts.note: airs are tunes, not pretensions: someone without melody rather than without conceit

explanation.surface: A modest person who does not put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving oneself airs' means being conceited, but airs are also melodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking melody, out of key.

clue.text: " Then come kiss me, sweet and. — " (T Night)

definitions.text: " Then come kiss me, sweet and. — " (T Night)

parts.words: " Then come kiss me, sweet and. — " (T Night)
parts.note: a gap-fill from Feste's song in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, 'O mistress mine'

explanation.surface: A line from a Shakespeare love song.
explanation.walkthrough: Feste sings 'Then come kiss me, sweet and twenty, Youth's a stuff will not endure' in Twelfth Night, Act 2.
explanation.definitionFit: The number completing the line, meaning a sweetheart of that age.
